Henry Kissinger's secret trip to China took place from 9 to 11 July 1971, when the United States national security adviser flew to Beijing to meet Premier Zhou Enlai and prepare a visit by President Richard Nixon.

The two countries had no ties since 1949. Messages were passed through several channels, and Pakistan's ruler Yahya Khan was the most important. During a tour of Asia, Kissinger pretended to be ill while in Pakistan and was flown secretly to Beijing. On 15 July Nixon announced on television that he would visit China.

The visit followed in February 1972 (see Nixon's visit to China). It split the Communist world, since Mao's China and the Soviet Union already distrusted each other, and it changed the balance of the Cold War.

It also had a cost. Washington's need for Yahya's help is one reason it stayed silent over the killings in Bangladesh. Soon afterward India signed a treaty with Moscow.
sum: Henry Kissinger's secret trip to China took place from 9 to 11 July 1971, when the United States national security adviser flew to Beijing to meet Premier Zhou Enlai and prepare a visit by President Richard Nixon.
